subject: SLO workshop: p95/p99 targets, streaming & concurrency clarifications
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Mercer <alex@brightleaf.ai>, ops-team@brightleaf.ai
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.inference>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-05-29T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: SLO workshop: p95/p99 targets, streaming & concurrency clarifications

Hi Alex / Brightleaf ops team,

Thanks again for the call earlier — useful to see your production envelope and the areas you'd like us to validate. Short recap and concrete asks so we can scope a hosted qualification run: 

- Agreed target envelope for evaluation (your ask): end-to-end p95 = ~120 ms, p99 = <= 380 ms for chat completions (including routing + auth). You flagged spikes during peak hours; we noted occasional p99s above 1s in their traces.
- Workload profile: sustained baseline of ~200 QPS with up to ~50 QPS burst windows for 3–8 minutes. Mix is ~70% short prompts (<50 tokens) and ~30% long context requests (200–800 tokens). Streaming enabled for conversation UX (partial chunks every ~200–400ms).

Action items we need from Brightleaf to scope the hosted test: 
1) Real traffic CSV (timestamps, effective payload size, request type label) for a representative 24–48h window so we can reproduce arrival patterns.
2) 10–20 sample request payloads (JSONL) covering short/long streaming and non-streaming cases — include headers you send (auth, customer-id, any custom compression).
3) Confirmation on whether you need preserved client IPs (whitelisting) for network egress; if so, provide CIDR list.
4) The current provider's recent latency traces (p95/p99 per minute) and an example end-to-end trace for a slow request (server timestamps). An attachment stub is fine.

What Redwood will deliver for the hosted qualification: 
- 48-hour canary run against Redwood hosted API (not production switchover) reproducing your traffic envelope. We'll measure p95/p99 end-to-end and componentized latency (auth, routing, model inference, streaming flush).
- Suggested config: prefix/KV cache warm-up, continuous batching disabled for streaming paths, quantified concurrency slices for long-context requests.
- A short runbook + test endpoint and sandbox API key for the window.

Please attach the CSV + sample requests and a representative slow trace. If we get those today/tomorrow we can schedule a canary for early next week.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

(attachments: current_provider_latency_logs.tsv [tsv], sample-requests.jsonl [jsonl])

From: Alex Mercer <alex@brightleaf.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.inference>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.inference>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-05-30T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLO workshop: p95/p99 targets, streaming & concurrency clarifications

Thanks, Irene — good summary. Quick clarifications from our side: 

- Our observed numbers on current provider (prod telemetry): p95 ~ 320 ms, p99 ~ 1.2 s over the last 7 days (see attached minute-level export). Those p99 spikes correlate with long-context ticketing payloads (500–800 tokens) and periodic backend batching.
- Streaming detail: we flush partial segments every ~300 ms on the server side; client expects partial token delivery so end-to-end perceived latency matters more than model-only latency.
- Cache behavior: we do not use a warmed KV cache consistently; long-tail sessions often miss. We'd welcome Redwood's warm-up recommendations.

We can provide: 48h traffic CSV, 20 sample payloads, and our procurement team can share IP ranges if required. Proposed canary window: June 6–7 (PST). Procurement (procure@brightleaf.ai) copied for scheduling and PO questions.

I'll attach the minute-level latency export and a short trace for the slow-case.

—Alex
VP, Platform Engineering
Brightleaf AI

(attachments: provider-sample-traces.zip [zip], brightleaf-requested-traffic.csv [csv])

From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Mercer <alex@brightleaf.ai>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.inference>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-05-31T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLO workshop: p95/p99 targets, streaming & concurrency clarifications

Alex — thanks for the artifacts, helpful. A few engineering clarifications so we can size the hosted run deterministically: 

- Traffic reproduction: CSV should include at minimum: epoch(ms), request_type(short|long|stream), payload_bytes, client_customer_id. If you can flag which requests were retried by the client that helps (retry_count).
- Concurrency envelope: we need per-second concurrency distribution rather than just QPS. Specifically: % of seconds with concurrency > 50, > 100, > 200. That influences worker shard sizing.
- Sequence length distribution: token counts after tokenization are ideal. If you can't re-tokenize for us, send raw char/word counts and we can approximate.
- Streaming semantics: confirm chunk boundary contract — do you send final "done" marker or rely on TCP FIN? Also include your average chunk size in bytes and whether you use SSE or chunked HTTP/2.
- Auth/headers: include an example header set (we rarely need to reproduce auth, but knowing header sizes helps).

Operational requests from Redwood for the canary: 
1) Approval to run synthetic traffic that mimics your CSV from Redwood-hosted IPs for an isolated sandbox key.
2) A signed NDA addendum for log retention if we need to store traces beyond 30 days (optional but often requested for postmortems).

Deliverables from us for the canary: test endpoint + sandbox key, smoke-test runbook (attached), and an automated post-run report with component-level latency and throughput curves.

I attached the draft runbook. If those CSV fields are feasible we'll provision the sandbox and draft a simple k6/locust job to mirror your arrival pattern.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

(attachments: redwood-smoke-test-runbook.pdf [pdf])

From: Alex Mercer <alex@brightleaf.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.inference>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-06-01T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLO workshop: p95/p99 targets, streaming & concurrency clarifications

Logan / Irene — attaching the requested CSV and traces. Confirming June 6–7 window works for us for the 48-hour canary. We can provide CIDR list for whitelisting (will send in separate email from procurement).

Also answering your streaming question: we use chunked HTTP/2 with an explicit final 'event: done' marker; average chunk size ~1.2 KB (mostly UTF-8). Retries are client-driven, retry_count included in the CSV.

Procurement looped in: Procure has a standard sandbox MSA; they can sign the NDA addendum early next week.

We look forward to the run — please share the sandbox key and test endpoint once provisioned.

—Alex
VP, Platform Engineering
Brightleaf AI

(attachments: brightleaf-requested-traffic.csv [csv], provider-sample-traces.zip [zip])
